patients.summary: Retired police officer with long-standing, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes on metformin and basal-bolus insulin, and epilepsy on phenytoin, who joins in 2020 and develops a run of diabetic neuropathy diagnoses (painful sensorimotor, neurogenic bladder, autonomic). Recurrent UTIs follow self-catheterization, and a 2025 course of TMP-SMX tips him into phenytoin toxicity. Lifestyle change in 2024 brings his A1c to about 7.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 56, establishing care. Moving his care here after years at another office; records release signed today.

DM2: diagnosed around 2009. Takes metformin 1000 twice a day, glargine 24 units at night and lispro on a sliding scale with meals. Admits control has never been good. Checks sugars most mornings, numbers mostly 150s-200s by his report. No lows that he knows of.

Feet: about 4 months of burning and pins-and-needles in both feet, worse once he's in bed. Has tried Tylenol and ibuprofen, neither does much.

Seizure disorder: on phenytoin 300 mg daily for many years, prescribed by his old PCP. Can't recall his last seizure, it's been that long.

NKDA. No surgeries. Quit cigarettes ~20 yrs ago, about 10 pack-years. Has never drunk alcohol. Retired from police work.
FHx: father had type 2 diabetes and an MI at 62. Mother: HTN, kidney disease from diabetes. A sibling had diabetes in pregnancy.

Exam: BP and pulse as recorded. Well appearing, pleasant. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: skin intact, no ulcers, pulses 2+ DP bilaterally. Reduced sensation to monofilament at the toes both sides.

A/P
1. DM2, uncontrolled by history. A1c, CMP, CBC, lipids, urine albumin today. Continue current regimen for now.
2. Burning feet, likely diabetic neuropathy. Referring to endocrinology for neuropathy eval and help with the insulin regimen.
3. Epilepsy, controlled. Phenytoin level with labs. Continue 300 mg daily.
4. Health maintenance: hep C and HIV screen once. PHQ-2 negative. Will get prior records for colonoscopy and vaccine history. Flu shot in the fall.
Return in about 3-4 months, after endocrinology.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Brooks, your labs are back. A1c is 8.0%, which is above where we want it but it gives us a starting point. Kidney function, blood counts and thyroid are normal, and your phenytoin level is in range. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. I sent the endocrinology referral; their office should call you to schedule.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy
Diabetic motor neuropathy
conditions.note: motor component of sensorimotor polyneuropathy; diminished ankle reflexes

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 10/23/2020
Referred by: primary care, for painful feet and diabetes management

Thank you for sending Mr. Brooks, a 57-year-old man with type 2 diabetes since about 2009 on metformin plus glargine and lispro, and epilepsy on phenytoin.

He has had burning and tingling in both feet for roughly six months. It is worst at night. He calls the pain sharp, like an electric jolt, and at times it climbs into the lower legs. No injury and no recent medication changes. Acetaminophen and ibuprofen have helped very little.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID; insulin glargine 24 units qHS; insulin lispro sliding scale with meals; phenytoin 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker (quit ~20 yrs, 10 pk-yr), no alcohol, retired law enforcement.
Family: father T2DM and MI at 62; mother hypertension and diabetic nephropathy; sibling with gestational diabetes.

Exam: Alert, comfortable. Feet without ulceration or deformity. Light touch and pinprick reduced in a stocking-glove pattern. Ankle jerks diminished bilaterally. Strength full in the lower extremities.

Lab: HbA1c 7.8% today.

Impression:
1. Painful, symmetric distal diabetic polyneuropathy of the lower extremities, sensorimotor, with a motor component (reduced ankle reflexes) consistent with diabetic motor neuropathy.
2. Type 2 diabetes, suboptimally controlled.

Recommendations: Continue present insulin and metformin doses. Daily foot inspection and proper footwear reviewed. Will see him back as needed; happy to reassess at any time.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Consult received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Endo letter reviewed. Neuropathy dx added to problem list. Will go over at his December visit.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after endocrinology.
S: Saw endo in October; their note came in last month. A1c there 7.8. Feet still burn at night, unchanged. He takes acetaminophen most evenings. No new symptoms. Insulin doses unchanged; morning sugars 140s-190s.
O: Vitals as charted. Feet: no skin breakdown, monofilament reduced distally both feet.
A/P
- DM2 with painful polyneuropathy and motor component per endo. Continue metformin, glargine 24 u, lispro scale. Foot care reviewed again. A1c next spring.
- Epilepsy, stable on phenytoin.
RTC 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About four months of having to wait for the stream to start, and it's weak when it comes. Feels like he doesn't fully empty. Some dribbling after. No pain with urination, no blood, no fever. Night trips about twice. Sugars running higher this winter, 180s-250s, less walking with the weather.
O: Vitals as charted. Abdomen soft, nontender, no obvious distension. Deferred prostate exam today at his request, will leave to urology.
A/P
1. Voiding difficulty with incomplete emptying in a man with diabetic neuropathy. Concern for retention/bladder dysfunction vs prostate. UA, PSA, BMP. Urology referral.
2. DM2, A1c result pending. Continue regimen; we talked about getting back to walking.
RTC after urology.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your urine test showed no infection and your PSA and kidney tests are normal. The A1c came back at 9.4%, higher than last fall. Let's keep working on it at your next visit. Urology has your referral.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Saw urology in late April. He says they checked how much was left in his bladder after voiding, said it was a lot, and called it a nerve problem of the bladder from the diabetes. They taught him to self-cath, he's doing it twice a day and getting the hang of it. Stream no better but he feels emptier. No urinary infection symptoms. We have not received a note from urology.
Sugars: still high, mostly 170-240.
O: Vitals as charted. Abd soft. Feet unchanged.
A/P
1. Neurogenic bladder per urology (patient report), on intermittent self-catheterization. Records request sent to urology. Will need catheter supplies paperwork.
2. DM2, A1c 9.1 today. Discussed adding to his regimen vs better adherence to the lispro scale. He'd like to work on meals and the scale first. Revisit in fall.
3. Epilepsy stable.
RTC 3-4 months.

conditions.label: Neurogenic bladder
conditions.note: diabetic; post-void residual 300 mL; on clean intermittent self-catheterization

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 04/26/2021
Reason for referral: voiding difficulty

57 y/o M with T2DM, painful diabetic polyneuropathy seen by endocrinology about six months ago, and epilepsy. For six months he has had hesitancy and a weak stream, a feeling that the bladder does not empty, and dribbling after he believes he is done. No hematuria, no dysuria.

Meds: metformin, insulin glargine, insulin lispro, phenytoin. Allergies: none known.
Surgical history: none.

Exam: Bladder palpable and percussible above the pubic symphysis. Genitalia normal. Prostate smooth, normal size, without nodules.
Bladder scan post-void residual: 300 mL.

Assessment: Incomplete emptying with an elevated residual in the setting of long-standing diabetic neuropathy, consistent with neurogenic bladder.
Plan: Clean intermittent self-catheterization taught in clinic; he demonstrated good technique. Catheterize twice daily, more if he feels full. Supplies to be ordered through his PCP. Return as needed.

Urology

documents.title: Urology note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Urology note finally arrived. PVR 300, neurogenic bladder, CIC BID. Matches what he told us. Problem list updated.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial annual wellness visit.
Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives independently, manages own meds and insulin. No falls in the past year. Hearing and vision OK by his report; due for eye exam, encouraged to schedule with his optometrist. PHQ-2 0. Cognition: no concerns, recall 3/3.
Current problems: DM2 with painful sensorimotor polyneuropathy, neurogenic bladder on CIC, epilepsy.
Meds reviewed and reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 24 u qHS, lispro scale, phenytoin 300 daily, acetaminophen prn.
Screening: colonoscopy 2014 normal (due 2024). Hep C/HIV done 2020. Not a lung screening candidate (10 pack-years).
Vaccines: PCV20 and first Shingrix today. Flu next month. COVID primary series done.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart and lungs unremarkable. Feet: intact skin, reduced monofilament distally.
Labs: CMP, lipids, urine albumin, phenytoin level.
Advance directive: will think about a health care proxy; form given.
Shingrix #2 in 2 months.

results.text: No Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter or Shiga toxin-producing organisms isolated

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About four weeks of loose, watery stools, several a day, sometimes urgent. No blood, no black stool, no fever. No travel, no new foods, no antibiotics this year. Appetite okay. No one sick at home.
O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses.
A/P
1. Diarrhea x 4 weeks. Stool culture today. Given duration, will send to GI for colonoscopy; his last one was 2014. Hydration reviewed; watch sugars with any change in eating.
2. Flu vaccine today.
Call if fever, bleeding, or he can't keep up with fluids.

documents.title: RE: Stool test

documents.title: Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second shingles vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Series complete. Pt reports he got a COVID booster at the pharmacy on 11/5; added to immunization record. Prep instructions for colonoscopy reviewed with him, including holding metformin and adjusting insulin the day before as GI instructed.

reports.text: Indication: diarrhea for two months. Prep: good. Cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve identified; terminal ileum intubated briefly and appeared normal. The colonic mucosa was normal throughout, without inflammation, ulceration or mass. No polyps. No diverticula. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
reports.conclusion: Normal colonoscopy. No structural or inflammatory cause for diarrhea found.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
COLONOSCOPY
Date of procedure: 11/29/2021
Referring: primary care
Allergies: NKDA
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care, tolerated well.
Findings: normal colon to the cecum and a short look at the terminal ileum. No inflammation, no polyps.
Impression: normal study. No structural explanation for his diarrhea. Suggest continued evaluation with his PCP; diabetes-related bowel dysmotility is a consideration.
Next colonoscopy for screening: 10 years.
Gastroenterology

events.reason: Ongoing diarrhea, bloating, lightheaded after meals

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic (poly)neuropathy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
58M with DM2, painful polyneuropathy and neurogenic bladder, f/u diarrhea.
S: Diarrhea now about 3 months and he'd call it severe, several loose stools a day. Bloated after he eats, and he gets lightheaded after meals, has to sit down for a bit. No travel, no antibiotics. No fever, no blood, weight about the same.
Data: stool culture 10/22 negative. Colonoscopy 11/29 normal, no inflammation or structural lesion. A1c 8.9 from last week (down from 9.1).
O: Vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft and nontender, bowel sounds mildly hypoactive, no distension or masses. Feet: pinprick reduced both feet.
A/P
1. Diarrhea with bloating and postprandial lightheadedness, negative workup, in long-standing poorly controlled DM with known neuropathy. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy involving gut and cardiovascular system. Added to problem list.
   - Smaller, more frequent meals, lower fat; keep fluids up.
   - Sit or lie a few minutes after larger meals, get up slowly.
   - Keep a log of stools and sugars.
2. DM2: A1c 8.9, slowly better. Same regimen.
3. Neurogenic bladder: CIC going fine. No UTIs.
RTC 3 months, sooner if worse.
